content.title: About
content.content: Chicken cream soup is a thick, velvety puree‑style soup made from chicken fillet, broth, cream, and aromatic spices. It has a mild buttery flavor with a subtle chicken note and a silky texture, perfect as a starter on a cold day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken cream soup emerged in the early 20th century as a haute‑cuisine dish in Europe.
Traditionally it is prepared from chicken broth, cream, and pureed cooked vegetables such as potato, carrot, and onion.
In Russia its popularity rose after canned versions appeared in the 1950s.
The soup is often served with croutons, fresh herbs, or grated cheese.
Many variations exist: with mushrooms, corn, spinach, or ginger.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The soup supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Chicken and vegetables deliver iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The pureed texture and gentle cooking make the soup easy on the stomach, beneficial during colds.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: The broth provides fluids and electrolytes, helping maintain proper hydration.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or eggs and should avoid the product.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream adds calories and saturated fat, so portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Prepared cream soups often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can allow bacterial growth, so cool the soup quickly and keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, bringing it to a gentle boil. Garnish with croutons, fresh herbs, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil. For a lighter version, replace cream with low‑fat yogurt or milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished cream soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze it in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to a boil before serving.
